full_judgment: 6. There is no definition of capital machinery under the Customs Act and no other notification has been issued under the Act. Machinery is classified in section XVI of the First Schedule of the Customs Act in Chapters 84 and 85. In the absence of definition, the general rules for the interpretation of the harmonized system of classification of goods in the nomenclature framed in exercise of powers under section 18 of the Customs Act shall hold the field. There is no doubt that the machineries were manufactured in 1986-87, 1988, 1989, 1990, 1995, 1996 and 1997. If these machineries fall within the classification of vehicles, then they being more than four years old are restricted items as per HS Code heading 87.01 to 87.04 of appendix-1 and footnote 1.4 of the Import Policy 2003-06. They are restricted items and liable to confiscation under section 16 of the Customs Act read with section 3(3) of the Import and Export (Control) Act, 1950. However, if the imported consignments are found to be capital machineries, it will not be contraband items and the machineries having ten years longevity were importable items for the use of industries.
